ingredients.name: Sweetened condensed milk
ingredients.notes: 1 standard tin (397g/14oz); do not use evaporated milk

ingredients.name: Caster or granulated sugar
ingredients.notes: 1 cup; dissolved in water before adding condensed milk

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: 1/2 cup; used to dissolve the sugar first

ingredients.name: Cashew nuts
ingredients.notes: dry-roasted and coarsely chopped; added near the end

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter
ingredients.notes: adds richness and gloss; added near the end

ingredients.name: Vanilla extract
ingredients.notes: optional but widely used in modern recipes; add at the very end off the heat

steps.instruction: Grease an 8x8 inch (20x20cm) baking pan with butter. Line with parchment paper and grease again. Keep a buttered knife and spatula nearby -- you'll need them quickly at the end.

In a large, heavy-bottomed pan (at least 3x the volume of your ingredients -- the mixture can bubble up), combine the sugar and water. Cook over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely.
Add the condensed milk and stir to combine. Add a pinch of salt. Turn the heat to medium-low. From this point, stir continuously -- do not walk away from the pan.

Continue cooking and stirring constantly over medium-low heat for 35-45 minutes. The mixture will gradually thicken and deepen in colour from pale cream to a deep golden brown. Do not increase the heat to speed this up -- it will burn.

Test for doneness: drop a small amount into a glass of cold water -- it should form a soft, pliable ball (soft ball stage, about 116C/240F on a thermometer). Alternatively, the mixture is ready when it leaves the sides of the pan cleanly and holds its shape briefly when a spoon is dragged through it.
Add the butter, vanilla extract (if using), and chopped cashews. Stir quickly to combine.
Working fast, pour and scrape the hot toffee mixture into the prepared pan. Spread evenly with a buttered spatula. Score into squares or rectangles immediately with a buttered knife before it sets.

Leave at room temperature for at least 1 hour until fully set and firm. Cut along the score lines. Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks, separating layers with parchment paper.

source_site: hungrylankan.com, cross-checked against sbs.com.au, rnz.co.nz, milkmaid.lk, infolanka.com, vinitasfamilyblog.blogspot.com, foodhow.com, and deliciousrecipebook.com
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 8+ independent sources; highest trust score for a sweet/confection in this collection due to unusually strong agreement on technique across both Sri Lankan and international sources
notes: Sri Lankan milk toffee (kiri toffee) is the most universally loved and widely made traditional Sri Lankan sweet -- eaten year-round, not just at New Year, and one of the first things Sri Lankans overseas make when feeling homesick. The dish is essentially a variant of fudge or penuche, with condensed milk replacing cream. Three critical rules shared across all sources: (1) use a large, heavy-bottomed pan as the mixture bubbles up and can boil over; (2) stir constantly on medium-low heat without interruption for the entire 35-45 minute cook time; (3) do not increase heat to hurry it -- this causes burning and a bitter result. A candy thermometer removes the guesswork: soft ball stage is 116C/240F. The vanilla taxonomy entry is repurposed from 'ing_sugar' for consistency with earlier dessert entries; a dedicated 'ing_vanilla' entry should be added to the taxonomy for future dessert recipes.
